transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Democrats seized control of the next Congress from Republicans in yesterday's midterm elections.
They won seven additional U.S. Senate seats, with two Senate races still outstanding in
Alaska and Mississippi.
Democrats won an additional 25 House seats over what they had previously, with dozens
of races yet to be called.
Democrat Abdul El Sayed won Michigan's open Senate seat over Republican challenger Mike
Rogers.
El Sayed says voters want Democrats to focus on the economy and not on President Trump's
priorities.
I think this is a mandate to take on Trumpism and address the crisis of affordability that
we're facing in our lives.
People understand that Donald Trump has not just addressed the affordability issues in
their lives.
He's made them worse.
You think about this illegal, unjustifiable war in Iran.
You think about this tariff policy, a tariff war with Canada.
We're paying huge at the gas pump.
We're paying huge at the grocery store.
We're paying $5,600 a year here in Michigan because of his Canadian tariff policy.
And then there's the imminent threat of the Medicaid cuts that are just around the corner.
So this is about standing up to build a more affordable America by standing up to Trump
and Trumpism.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
The midterm elections yesterday saw huge swings toward Democratic candidates in key races,
especially in the South.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports much of that is from increased black voter turnout.
North and South Carolina flipped U.S. Senate seats.
Georgia elected a Democratic governor, the first black woman to hold that office in U.S.
history.
And in Alabama, Congressman Shamari Figgars held on in a district gerrymander to limit
black voting power.
The Senate race in Mississippi, a state that voted for Trump by 24 points and has the highest
share of black voters in the country, is too close to call.
It's not just federal races.
Democrats took control of several state legislative chambers and flipped seats across the region.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Republican political strategist Alex Conant worked for former President George W. Bush.
Conant says that there were similar economic issues 20 years ago when Republicans lost
midterm elections.
This was a referendum on Trump.
Trump wanted it to be a referendum on him.
Democrats wanted to be a referendum on him.
And that's what it was.
And then if you look at the exit polls, Trump's not popular.
People aren't happy with the direction of the economy.
They're not happy with the war, gas prices.
It was really a referendum, I think, on him and some of his policies, including tariffs
and the war in Iran.
It'll be interesting to see if there's any sort of course correction.
Bush doubled down.
He doubled down on the war after 2006 with the surge.
It'll be interesting to see what Trump does now if he also doubles down.
I suspect he will.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
There were few hiccups reported at polling sites yesterday.
There were weather-related problems in Florida.
Some polling stations were relocated because of flooding.
This is NPR.
Today, Israel is publishing final results of its own elections held last week, but incumbent
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has questioned these results.
NPR's Lauren Freire reports from Tel Aviv.
Prime Minister Netanyahu's party fell short of a parliamentary majority, and he has since
sought to discredit the results, alleging Arab voter fraud and foreign interference.
But Israel's Central Elections Committee says all complaints have been examined and
that there's no evidence of any irregularities.
Netanyahu's party nevertheless abstained from certifying the results.
Netanyahu's president meanwhile is meeting one by one with leaders of the country's various
political parties to decide who to tap to form a coalition government.
The president's consultations are being live-streamed and are expected to last through Thursday.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Investigators in Florida say they have located a piece of the small business jet that crashed
into a neighborhood last weekend.
The fuselage chunk was discovered miles from the crash site near Palm Beach.
The accident killed nine people aboard the jet.
Authorities say they've determined the Lear jet had started to break up before it crashed.
Tennessee authorities say a convicted murderer who escaped prison has been recaptured.
Jacob Morley has been on the lam for about 10 days.
He was picked up near Kansas City, Missouri by troopers after his truck got stuck in the
mud.
Morley is supposed to be serving a life sentence in Tennessee for killing a co-worker four
years ago.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Democrats win Senate seats and House majority in midterms, with Alaska and Mississippi races pending
Abdul El Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat over Republican Mike Rogers, citing affordability
Midterm results show big Democratic gains in South, driven by increased Black voter turnout
Republican strategist Alex Conant says midterms were a referendum on Trump's economy, war, and tariffs
Few polling site problems reported, including weather-related relocations in Florida due to flooding
Israel publishes final election results; Netanyahu disputes them and his party abstains from certifying
Investigators recover jet fuselage piece miles from Palm Beach, Florida crash that killed nine
Tennessee convicted murderer Jacob Morley recaptured near Kansas City after escaping prison
